CS 510

Wireless and Network Security

  • Graduate
  • 3 credits

Offered: Spring 2026

This course covers the security of distributed systems and wired and wireless networks. Students learn to evaluate protocols, design appropriate controls, and reason about the resilience and operation of networked systems.

Selected Topics

  • IEEE 802.11 security, wireless encryption, and authentication
  • Network key management, routing, switching, and segmentation
  • Intrusion detection, security monitoring, and denial-of-service resilience
  • Secure network architecture, incident response, and recovery

Learning Objectives

  • Explain security mechanisms for distributed and wireless systems.
  • Compare authentication, encryption, and key-management approaches.
  • Assess network security risks and propose detection, response, and design improvements.

Coursework & Projects

Applied assignments and a course project connect protocol and network design decisions to practical security scenarios. Quizzes and a midterm assess understanding.
